newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS-RMC share bears return as profit dives.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-RMC share bears return as profit dives.

text.p: British building materials giant RMC Group Plc on Thursday lived up to its doom-laden profit warning earlier this year by reporting a slump in half year profits and saying full year figures would fall short of 1995.
Pretax profits for the six months to June 30 fell 26.5 percent to 95.8 million pounds ($149.3 million), with sales sliding five percent to 2.11 billion. The dividend rose five percent to 7.8 pence.
The company blamed its performance on "the worst winter for 10 years" which delayed building projects and exacerbated already weak European markets, said chief executive Peter Young.
RMC said second half figures should be "satisfactory" but the full year was unlikely to match record 1995 earnings.
The profit slump had been predicted but investors were hoping for a better outlook, particularly in RMC's biggest market Germany.

Hopes that the worst had passed in Germany led RMC to hit a new year high this week at 1,199 pence. But with those hopes dashed, the market bears returned, taking the stock down 33 pence to 1,119-1/2 pence.
The outlook for Europe was described as mixed, with more bad news on Germany, which contributed 40 percent of profits and sales last year.
"I don't want to be too optimistic about Germany. There may be a slight decline in volumes of one or two percentage points (in 1997)," Young told Reuters
Building spending has been hit by tighter fiscal control as the German government seeks to meet the criteria for European Monetary Union.
Young said the French market would "remain at the bottom." But he was more upbeat on Britain where the housing market pick-up was just beginning to feed through to the new house sector.
"It will not be a bonanza. But there will be some improvement," he said.
The reaction from analysts was downbeat.

"It is looking a bit bleak," said Robin Hardy at Panmure Gordon. "The decline in Germany is quite severe and the company's statement gives no great hope that things will be better in the second half."
Andrew Melrose at Paribas Capital markets summed up the gloom, saying: "This is not a temporary hiccup."
A breakdown of the results shows German sales fell to 733 million pounds from 882 million, with profits collapsing to 28 million from 65 million.
Britain saw sales edge up to 554 million from 551 million, but profits fell to 33 million from 39 million.
Other European countries saw sales fall to 517 million from 528 million, with profits down to 24 million from 27 million.
Countries ouside of Europe saw sales of 310 million versus 267 million, with profits of 110 million versus 151 million. ($1=.6415 Pound)
